title: Notes on a reading loop
plain:
Notes on a reading loop

Most reading tools optimise for collecting. The loop that matters is smaller: something arrives, you decide in a few seconds whether it is worth your attention today, and the ones that are get read to the end.

Three rules held up over a year. Decide once: an item is read, queued or dismissed, never left hovering. Read in the tool: the moment you leave for a browser tab, the decision is lost. Keep what you finish: the library is the record of what you actually read, not what you meant to.

The agent's job in this loop is narrow. It explains a passage, checks a claim against what you kept, or rebuilds a page the extractor mangled. It does not decide for you.
